name: Expose existing plugin abilities to Claude Desktop via MCP
query: My plugin already registers a few abilities via wp_register_ability — things like 'list pending comments', 'approve comment', 'mark as spam'. I want to expose them to Claude Desktop so I can moderate comments by talking to Claude. The site is on WordPress 7.1. What do I install, and what do I need to change about my abilities to make this work cleanly?
expected_behavior: Step 1: Run wordpress-router to classify repo kind
Step 2: Run wp-project-triage to detect plugin structure
Step 3: Route to wp-abilities-api skill (point at references/mcp-exposure.md)
Step 4: Check the runtime before installation: MCP Adapter 0.6.x requires WordPress 6.9+ and PHP 7.4+; on PHP 7.2 or 7.3, stop and upgrade the runtime or do not enable MCP exposure
Step 5: Install the canonical MCP Adapter plugin (release zip / wp plugin install), not a bundled Composer copy — 0.6.x deprecated bundling and emits _deprecated_function() when loaded as a library

Step 6: Declare the dependency with a Requires Plugins: mcp-adapter header, and note it does not resolve yet because the adapter is not on WordPress.org (#178), so add a class_exists() guard plus an admin notice
Step 7: Explain that exposure resolves through McpAbilityExposure::is_public() — an explicit meta.mcp.public wins, an absent one inherits meta.public, and malformed meta.mcp fails closed
Step 8: Warn that WordPress 7.1 added meta.public and marks every core ability public, so on 7.1 + adapter 0.6+ the core abilities already reach the default MCP server without anyone opting in
Step 9: Set meta.mcp.public explicitly on each ability in both directions — true to expose, false to keep a REST-public ability off MCP — rather than relying on inheritance

Step 10: Audit existing abilities for proper meta.annotations: 'list pending comments' should be readonly:true, 'approve' should NOT be readonly (it mutates), 'mark as spam' should be destructive:true
Step 11: Ensure every ability has a permission_callback (especially destructive ones); MCP clients act as authenticated users
Step 12: Raise the default server's capability floors — discover/get/execute and the HTTP transport all default to 'read', which every Subscriber holds
Step 13: Set up an Application Password for the Claude Desktop user; explain Settings → Permalinks must NOT be Plain
Step 14: Verify by hitting /wp-json/ for the namespace and connecting Claude Desktop to confirm tools appear
Step 15: Use a custom server, mcp_adapter_default_server_config, or mcp_adapter_create_default_server when the integration needs an explicit ability allow-list or a tools/resources/prompts split
success_criteria: Routes to wp-abilities-api with mcp-exposure.md reference
Stops on PHP 7.2 or 7.3 and states the WordPress 6.9+ / PHP 7.4+ floor for MCP Adapter 0.6.x
Recommends installing the canonical MCP Adapter plugin and does not recommend bundling it via Composer
Uses a Requires Plugins header and notes it does not resolve until the adapter is listed on WordPress.org
Audits annotations: readonly for read operations, destructive for spam/delete
Confirms permission_callback on all abilities (especially destructive ones)
States that meta.mcp.public is inherited from meta.public when absent on MCP Adapter 0.6+
Does not claim that omitting meta.mcp.public keeps an ability off MCP
Warns that WordPress 7.1 core abilities are public and therefore already exposed through the default server
Sets meta.mcp.public explicitly, including false to opt a public ability out
Does not claim the default server exposes every registered ability regardless of exposure metadata
Keeps permission_callback enforcement separate from public discovery metadata
Raises the 'read' capability floors on the default server before production use
Mentions Application Passwords as the practical local-dev auth method
